# Marker

A divider or status line inside a conversation, such as a date or someone joining.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## See it live

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Dividing a long conversation into days, in plain words. Not a message someone wrote.

- **Use it when:** Breaking a long conversation into days or showing events in it.
- **Not when:** A message someone wrote.

Instead:

- [Message](./message.md): Something someone said.

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Look closer

<div class="odv-anat-link"><a href="./marker-anatomy">Anatomy reference →</a><span>Each part of Marker, and how the design decisions reach it: the answer, the rule, the token and the value you see.</span></div>

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add marker
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Marker reads 4 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Marker's tokens to change Marker alone.
